text:
alex: quick sync — I'm refactoring TF modules for service-auth across infra. I moved the auth module into modules/security and hoisted provider blocks. CI terraform plan shows provider version drift vs root lockfile, can someone eyeball before I open the PR? plan excerpt below.

alex: ```
Terraform will perform the following actions:
  # module.security.kubernetes_secret.auth will be updated in-place
  ~ resource "kubernetes_secret" "auth" {
      ~ data = {
          - "token" = (sensitive) -> null
        }
    }
Releasing changes to providers: registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes: 2.7.0 -> 4.0.1
```

maria: can you paste the infra repo link + full plan log? :eyes:

alex: link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4125
plan log: ci/buildkite/infra-plan-4125.log (attached in CI artifacts). I ran `terraform init -upgrade` locally to reproduce.

chris: looks like one of the moved modules had looser constraints and picked kubernetes v4.0. we intentionally kept 2.x pinned in root. did you run `terraform providers lock` after the refactor?

alex: not yet — I did `init -upgrade` to test the module move but didn't regenerate the lockfile. I can revert the module constraint or pin it. also noticed k8s secret key name changed (auth -> auth-token) which will break the chart unless we wire a migration.

tanya: on the k8s side — is that in the overlays/kustomize or helmvalues? I can prepare a patch. If we change key names, we should provide a mapping and a zero-downtime rotation.

chris: for TF, suggestion: add explicit `required_providers` in the moved module (same versions we use in root) and run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` to generate updated lockfile, then commit only the lockfile update if it's expected. CI should fail if lockfile drift is detected.

alex: agreed. I'll update the module with `required_providers` and pin to the root-approved ranges (`kubernetes = "~> 2.7"`). I'll also add a small migration doc for the secret rename. Opening PR now.

devops-bot: plan completed for branch alex/refactor-auth — 1 planable change. Lockfile mismatch detected: modules/security/terraform.lock.hcl needs regeneration.

maria: I'll take a look in about an hour. alex — please add the migration steps in the PR description (kubectl commands + `kubectl rollout restart` guidance).

alex: done — PR description updated and added `migration.md` with commands:
```bash
# create rotated secret without downtime
kubectl create secret generic auth-rotated --from-literal=token=$(vault read -field=token secret/auth) -n svc
# patch deployment to reference new key then rotate back to canonical name
kubectl patch deploy svc-auth -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"auth-rotated":"true"}}}}}' -n svc
```

tanya: lgtm for the k8s part — tested similar flow on staging last week, should be safe. :thumbsup:

chris: reviewing TF now. small nit: rename module input `provider_alias` -> `auth_provider` for clarity and add a README in modules/security that lists supported provider versions and the lockfile generation steps. After that I'll approve.

alex: thanks — making those two edits now, will push and rerun CI.

maria: quick question — do we want a policy to block major provider upgrades in module moves? we've accidentally let a provider major jump slip through before.

chris: yes — I'll open a follow-up to add a tfsec/CI check that diffs `terraform providers` and fails the build if a major version increases.

alex: sweet. thx all. I'll ping again when CI is green and the migration steps are validated on staging.
